title: Kid Ory, Rod Cless and Ken Colyer as influences
summary: Ory's band with Howard and Cless's Spanier records strongly influenced him; Allen and Polites think Colyer sounds like Mutt Carey.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: What about Kit Orrie's band and what Kerry and those people, did they have any influence out there? Well, yes, they had a great influence on me.

I heard very early in the piece, I heard Kit Orrie band with Donald Howard, a session they made there, and I don't know why, I've heard Donald Howard several times since on record and he hasn't been impressive at all. On that particular record he was very impressive. I was particularly struck by it. In fact, I would say that probably, now I'm thinking of the answers to much earlier questions, Rod Kless with the Maxi Spania band was a strong influence on me because the Spania records were just coming out, I'd rush into the stores and get the new one that had come out each three months, they'd bring out a new one. Of that session, the 38 session, but they were coming out about 40, 41 in Australia.
And high school then, what we call high school.

Yes. Yes, I would have been. Rod Kless and then this Orrie session with Donald Howard, very free flowing sort of stuff, that had a great effect on me, yes. So that, but by and large I don't suppose the Orrie band did have any sort of great effect on any number of musicians.
Yeah, except maybe through Ken Collier, I feel that Mutt influenced him.

Collier, yes, I've always thought this, no one seems to say this very much, but I've always thought that he's a real Mutt type player. Well we talked about that, he and I, you know. Did he think that himself?
